title.en: Nature of matter: elements, compounds and mixtures

text.en: Poha and sprout salad both come from mixing ingredients. Is every kind of matter a mixture, or are some made of just one kind of substance?

A mixture is made of two or more substances that are mixed together but not chemically joined, like poha, salad or air.
The substances in a mixture keep their own properties and can be separated by simple methods like filtering, sieving or evaporation.
A pure substance has only one kind of particle and a fixed composition, such as water or iron.
An element is a pure substance that cannot be broken into simpler substances by chemical methods; examples are hydrogen, oxygen, iron and gold.
Each element has a symbol: H for hydrogen, O for oxygen, Fe for iron, Cu for copper, and Na for sodium.
A compound is a pure substance made of two or more elements chemically joined in a fixed ratio, like water, H₂O.
The properties of a compound differ from those of its elements: hydrogen and oxygen are gases but water is a liquid.
A compound can be broken into elements only by chemical methods, such as electricity splitting water.
Mixtures may be homogeneous like salt water or heterogeneous like sand in water, where parts can be seen.
Metals shine and conduct heat and electricity, while non-metals usually do not; this helps us classify elements.

problem.en: Classify: iron, water, air, sugar solution.

text.en: Air and sugar solution are mixtures.

prompt.en: How is a compound different from a mixture?

requiredIdeas.en: A compound has elements chemically joined in fixed ratio.
A mixture has substances only mixed.

commonMisconceptions.en: A mixture has a fixed formula.
A compound can be filtered apart.

points.en: Mixtures can be separated by physical methods.
Elements cannot be broken into simpler substances.
Compounds have elements chemically joined in a fixed ratio.
